real_class_family_mismatch_on_both_paths.limitation_disclosed: Both paths refuse, but in this tranche the refusal on both paths is produced by the tranche-local family ceiling rather than by the new coherence gate, because every constructible mismatch necessarily carries a non-authorable family. This was verified by deleting the registry coherence call and observing that the end-to-end test still passed. The coherence gate itself is proved by a behavioural decision test and a structural wiring test, each verified to fail when the gate is removed. No mismatch was faked to make the new gate look exercised.

regression_slice.method: Exact failure-ID set comparison on the same bounded three-court slice. The HQ214 court was run against the UNREPAIRED repair-base module (verified by sha256 to be exactly ade55043aaf33128708a672d1b23d1ef6f7b01c69e5b2ba080f6626847a9b33a), then against the repaired module, and the sorted ID sets were compared with comm. The module was file-swapped in place and restoration verified by sha256 after the swap, because a PYTHONPATH overlay does not shadow the pytest rootdir.

discriminating_versus_preservation_hones.note: Four of the new tests fail on the unrepaired module and pass on the repaired one; those carry the evidential weight. The remaining new tests pass on both: test_d1_authoring_refuses_a_genuine_class_family_mismatch and test_d1_registry_build_refuses_a_rehashed_hand_built_mismatched_rule pass on the base because the family ceiling already refused those pairs; test_d1_registry_build_still_accepts_a_coherent_pair, test_court_imports_no_refusal_vocabulary_from_production and the payload-helper tests are positive controls, structural or preservation witnesses. This is stated so a reviewer does not over-count the witness set.
